title: Streaming union resolver and schema-evolution helpers for Python SDK
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Streaming LLM outputs often emit incremental JSON that should hydrate to typed objects (pydantic/dataclasses). Many customers hit schema-evolution issues: field renames, union variants, and partial objects during streaming. Current SDK helpers assume stable shapes and either fail fast or force full-document parsing. This ticket implements a tolerant, ergonomic streaming union resolver plus schema-evolution hooks for the Python SDK.

Goals:
- Provide a streaming-friendly resolver to map incremental chunks into concrete typed variants (union members) without blocking full-stream assembly.
- Support an explicit schema version header and a registry of versioned deserializers for gradual evolution and rollbacks.
- Offer developer ergonomics: decorators / helper factories for common patterns (deprecated fields mapping, fallback constructors).
- Preserve retry semantics and idempotency: partial hydration must be resumable and safe under retries/backpressure.

Non-goals: full remote schema registry; complex migration tooling outside the SDK (we only provide lightweight local registries and hooks).
decisions: Support both pydantic and dataclass targets through a small adapter layer instead of forcing one representation.
Use a registry keyed by (type_name, schema_version) that maps to a lightweight deserializer callable.
Expose an opt-in strict_mode for customers who want raise-on-unrecognized-fields; default is tolerant with warnings.
Perform incremental parse of stream frames into a minimal shape-hint object before resolving a union member to reduce blocking.
Keep compatibility fallback behavior: older deserializers can be registered and tried in order when the exact version match fails.
Log and emit telemetry events (console + SDK trace) for unresolved unions and fallback selection to aid rollouts.
Do not rely on network calls during resolution; registry is local to the SDK process to avoid latency/regression.
Retry semantics: client-visible idempotency key is preserved on resume; hydrator checkpoints are stable across retries.
Expose simple migration helper functions (rename_field, coerce_type) as first-class, composable transformations.
Performance target: incremental parsing path adds <3% median CPU overhead for normal chat workloads (bench target).
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a StreamingUnionResolver API documented in the python-sdk README and examples.
Integration tests show correct resolution across three simulated schema-versions with fallbacks.
Streaming demo app hydrates union variants mid-stream and can resume from checkpoint after simulated retry.
Benchmarks for a 1k tokens/session workload show <3% overhead vs current baseline structured streaming path.
End-to-end example published in GitHub examples folder and referenced in SDK quickstart.
Telemetry events for fallback usage surface in Console (trace id included) for at least one rollout test.
Review and documentation of API ergonomics by DevRel and DX teams (sign-off comment in ticket).
